title: Automation Platform Support SLA Europe: Compared 2026
summary: Automation platform support SLA in Europe differs by vendor. Find response times and support windows these six offer so you can align with your needs.
body_markdown:
## One short verdict per platform


Where the vendor has written nothing, the verdict below reads "unconfirmed"; each one stops at what the vendor has put in writing.


### Zapier and Make


On its Professional plan, Zapier names a first-response time, counted in business hours. A business-hours clock means an outage on Friday evening waits until the working week resumes.


Lower plans carry no equivalent commitment in the material I can cite, so the commitment applies to Professional only.


We haven't confirmed Make's support terms. Ask for the page that ties a response time and a support-hours window to each plan, plus the EU hosting option in writing.


### n8n and Workato


You can run n8n as a hosted service or on your own servers, and support terms may differ between the two. Ask which deployment a stated response time covers. A commitment for the hosted plan says nothing about a self-hosted install.


Because Workato sells on enterprise contracts, the support terms most likely sit in the order form and not on a pricing page. Request the agreement and read the response-time and hours clauses. A sales call isn't a term.


### Power Automate and Activepieces


Because Power Automate's a Microsoft product, you may buy its support through a wider Microsoft support plan. If so, the response time belongs to that plan, not to the automation licence. Ask which plan your licence sits on.


We haven't confirmed Activepieces on response time, plan or support hours, and those stay unconfirmed until the vendor writes them down.


What a security review doesn't have to wait for is the MIT-licensed core: the source is public, so your team can read how jobs are queued and handed to workers, load-test it on its own hardware, and run it self-hosted or fully air-gapped before anyone signs.


MoneyGram and Moneypenny run Activepieces in production. A codebase you can inspect closes a review on evidence, where a closed vendor's word only reopens it.
